scattering amplitudes along Riemann surfaces constitute a fundamental element of quantum field theory. Within perturbative quantum chromodynamics (pQCD), these analytic amplitudes generate specific structures in the complex kinematical $s$-plane that impose rigorous constraints on perturbative calculations. These structures manifest as branch cuts and poles, yielding characteristic singularities in differential cross-sections that pQCD describes through logarithmic and non-analytic perturbative power laws. These features are ubiquitous in experimental data; for instance, pQCD successfully reconstructed the singularities in $D$-wave $\pi\pi$ scattering via their pseudo-Coulomb nucleon poles, explaining peaks in differential cross-sections. Similarly, recent findings in $\pi\pi$ and $KK$ scattering, along with their associated resonances, have been explained by such pole-based singularities. Although pQCD predictions regarding these phenomena are well-established, their direct experimental verification remains elusive. Previous attempts to detect these features in differential cross-sections were hampered by substantial systematic uncertainties. Current advances in LHC experimental capabilities now enable the precise measurement of multi-particle differential cross-sections with a resolution and granularity capable of resolving these singularities for the first time. Achieving this will significantly advance our comprehension of quantum field theories, a goal we advance by predicting the singularities expected from various multi-particle channels measurable at the LHC.

der Waals material NiI$_2$ are investigated using a combination of first-principles calculations and the dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). We find that while DMFT accurately reproduces the experimental Ni $d$-band width, it qualitatively misrepresents magnetic ordering, predicting NiI2 to be a Heisenbard metal with long-range order at zero temperature contrary to experiments which show NiI$_2$ to be an insulator with significant anisotropy and spiral magnetic ground state characterized by large Néel temperature. We attribute this failure to an artificial enhancement of DMFT-captured local correlations by the narrow Ni $d_{xy}$ sub-band, whose weight is not sufficiently screened by more itinerant $d_{xz}$ and $d_{yz}$ states in this specific system. To address this limitation, we propose a modified approach: the "energy-dependent DMFT" (ED-DMFT). This method assigns a separate self-energy to only those $d$-orbitals that are both dominant in constructing the experimental band structure and exhibit strong experimental quasiparticle weight. Preliminary tests indicate that applying this selective self-energy successfully restores the qualitative prediction of NiI$_2$ as an insulator with spiral magnetic anisototopy and stability near zero Kelvin, markedly improving agreement with experimental observations.

Furthermore, collecting such data manually is costly. This paper addresses the challenge of acquiring effect data through self-collection via an agent performing actions. We propose a novel approach utilizing natural language to bridge the gap between actions and effects in self-collected data. Specifically, we use a latent language model trained on natural language descriptions of effects found in standard datasets to instruct a variational autoencoder (VAE) trained on effect data. This model learns to generate effect descriptions from self-collected data based on their corresponding actions. Consequently, this latent language model can execute actions, predict effects through natural language, and bridge the connection between actions and effects in acquired data. We conducted experiments across three robotic manipulation tasks using a real-world data set. Results indicate that our method significantly surpasses existing baselines in predicting effects from self-collected actions and effectively estimates the quality of effect data gathered autonomously.

While existing work often focuses on analyzing attacks and defenses from a functional perspective, there is a growing need to examine these dynamics through an economic lens. This study introduces the novel *Adversarial Defense Game* (ADG), which models the strategic interactions between attackers and defenders, incorporating the costs and benefits associated with both sides. ADG allows for the modeling of diverse attack and defense strategies, enabling the evaluation of their efficacy under varying conditions. Analytically, the paper demonstrates that the game reaches a unique pure strategy Nash equilibrium, representing a stable pairing of specific attack and defense methods where mutual deviations are neither beneficial nor profitable. Empirical results using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets confirm the validity of ADG by modeling multiple attack and defense pipelines, successfully modeling their respective costs and gains within a broader economic framework.

This research introduces generalized ARKS specifically tailored to solve parabolic partial differential PAMs with separable spatial operators. By decoupling spatial and temporal discretizations, such PAMs can be reformulated as vector differential equations with separable structures, which these new GARKs can solve more efficiently than standard solvers designed for general differential equations. A key advantage of the proposed methods is their ability to achieve arbitrarily high temporal accuracy simply by increasing the count of independent computational stages. Furthermore, we demonstrate that when applied to linear problems, the methods generate a matrix structure amenable to efficient eigendecomposition. Leveraging this property allows us to reconstruct the full numerical solution with a far lower dimensionality and significantly reduced storage and computational demands. Finally, we present a series of test cases to illustrate the distinct benefits of this approach.

The primary aim of this research is to evaluate the potential of magnetotelluric (MT) data in identifying magnetized fluid fractures. This aim involves analyzing a subset of MT measurements from the 2014 M6.0 Iquique earthquake rupture zone in the Pacific coast of South America. The study focuses on a specific area measuring 20 km by 25 km, centered 20 km offshore and aligned with the earthquake's epicenter. The dataset comprises MT data from three distinct timeframes: two surveys conducted before a geological event and one survey performed after the 2014 earthquake. The research reveals that the post-seismic survey successfully captured a subsurface resistivity reduction along the primary surface rupture zone, which aligns with findings from other methodologies, such as radar interferometry and laser scanning. This lack of detection corresponds with the absence of certain features in radar and laser scan datasets, specifically those indicating deep-seated rock fracturing. This study introduces a fully automated framework designed to identify privacy violations across diverse data types, with a specific emphasis on social media content. By integrating various data sources and technologies, including social networks, web crawlers, public record databases, and services like Google Images, the proposed approach constructs comprehensive digital profiles for social entities. Utilizing electrostatic plasma gyrokinetic simulations, we establish a strong agreement with TRS burst characteristics observed in the NSTX, specifically the frequency, amplitude, and the $k_y$ wavevector peak. We attribute the TRS burst to the linear growth of ion temperature gradient (ITG) modes favored by the transient reversal of the toroidal magnetic field's curvature. Furthermore, we identify the nonlinear generation of zonal flows as a direct outcome of the ITG mode's geodesic acoustic mode (GAM) resonant instability. This mechanism is driven by the positive damping of the GAM in the low-frequency spectrum of the TRS burst. Consequently, this growth of zonal flows suppresses GAM amplitude and leads to the dissipation of the TRS burst. Additionally, the enhanced shearing rate produced by these zonal flows disrupts ITG mode activity, effectively terminating the burst. While the initial zonal flow spectrum resembles that of standard ITG modes, the final spectrum shifts toward lower wave numbers ($k_y$), mirroring behavior seen in other ITG scenarios. Although the present study attributes the observed NSTX activity to zonal flows, it remains possible that turbulent fluctuations also contribute to the signal.

breakthrough in understanding the underlying mechanisms behind color vision deficiency (CVD). This understanding has enabled the development of numerous machine learning tools designed to detect and classify the various forms of CVD. While existing literature thoroughly examines the underlying causes and symptoms of the different CVD types, very little attention has been given to understanding the commonalities shared among these conditions or exploring ways to create a unified detection and classification system capable of addressing all variants simultaneously. Understanding these condition synergies is vital for designing a comprehensive solution that manages the full spectrum of CVD. To this end, we introduce a novel deep convolutional neural network (DCNN) architecture designed for the unified identification and classification of all CVD forms. This approach was evaluated using a dataset comprising 15 distinct categories of CVD derived from retinal fundus images collected from 1,050 individuals. The model was trained to maximize the overlap in decision boundaries across all CVD classes to foster mutual understanding between the conditions. Our method achieved a mean per-class F1 score of 0.994, representing a significant improvement over traditional techniques that only detect and classify specific individual CVD types.

This study aimed to investigate the pathogenesis of CKD-TB and establish a diagnostic model. We constructed a rat model characterized by kidney vascular compression to simulate CKD-TB. Utilizing micro-CT scanning and histological analysis, we examined structural and tissue-level alterations. Furthermore, through advanced image analysis of these modalities, we developed a diagnostic model specific to this condition. Results indicated that while micro-CT analysis revealed significant structural abnormalities in the kidney vasculature, histological assessment showed corresponding pathological changes in the airways. Although the specific tissue origin of traction in TB remains debated, our findings demonstrate that vascular compression induces traction within the pulmonary parenchyma and associated blood vessels. Additionally, integrating micro-CT and histological data yielded a robust diagnostic model with strong explanatory power regarding tissue interactions in CKD-TB. These results clarify the tissue basis of traction bronchiectasis and provide a refined diagnostic framework, thereby enhancing understanding of the disease mechanism.
